newsitem.title: USA: IPAI data may hinder aluminum investment - Spector.
newsitem.headline: IPAI data may hinder aluminum investment - Spector.

text.p: The inclusion of China and Tajikistan under Asia in International Primary Aluminium Institute global metal production data may threaten investment in the sector as misleading figures could cause price volatility, industry analyst Stewart Spector said.

The decision by IPAI to lump in China and Tajikistan with Asia, instead of reporting them separately, has caused discontent among analysts, including Angus McMillan of Billiton, and James Southwood of Commodity Metals Management.

In his latest Aluminum Industry report, Spector reiterated there was no way to verify data from Tajikistan or from China, the latter with 62 primary aluminum smelters ranging from 5,000 to 30,000 tons of capacity.
IPAI Asia data in February showed a drop of 264,000 tons from January, a huge swing.
"The market's interpretation of misleading data also causes excessive price volatility, and facilitates market manipulation," Spector said.
The aluminum industry also needs to attract big sums of investment money.

"That alone is a good enough reason for the IPAI to clean up its statistical act. In a world where competition for capital is tough, producers should make it easier, not harder, for investors to understand what is really going on in the aluminum industry," Spector said.
Meanwhile, aluminum prices could reach $2,000 a tonne by June as stocks look likely to fall in the second quarter, Spector noted.
